title: Japan Airports Test Clothes-Shrinking Machines
paragraphs: Have you ever had trouble closing your suitcase at the end of a trip? Clothes can take up a lot of space — especially when you also have souvenirs to pack!

Luckily for souvenir-loving travelers — and the souvenir shops trying to sell them things — a Japanese clothing company called SJOY has created a machine that could help. The service is called Pocket Tips, and it compresses clothes to make them smaller.

Travelers put their clothes into the machine, and it automatically compresses them in about one minute, without using any plastic bags. Depending on the clothes, they can become small enough to fit in the palm of a person's hand — as little as one-seventh of their normal size.
Between September 2025 and January 2026, the machines were tested at four airports in Japan — Haneda and Narita in the Tokyo area, and Kumamoto and Naha, which are in the south of Japan.
During the tests, about 400 travelers also answered a survey. And around 70% said they had decided not to buy more souvenirs because they didn't have enough room in their luggage.
So Pocket Tips could help make both travelers and souvenir shops happier!
SJOY will now work with Haneda, Narita, Kumamoto and Naha airports as it prepares for a full launch of the service, although no start date has been announced yet.
SJOY says it may also look at using the service in hotels and clothing shops in the future.
